marks.gloss_en: אלא הכא במאי עסקינן -- במחופה עור: [an amulet] covered with leather (= p_okimta_mechupeh_or; attacked from tefillin at 62a.3 and defended at 62a.4 -- see obj_harei_tefillin)
rather, with what are we dealing here? with [an amulet] covered with leather
דאמר אביי: שין של תפילין הלכה למשה מסיני
התם משום שין -- there [they are removed] because of the shin (= p_tefillin_mishum_shin)
there [tefillin are removed] because of the shin
והרי תפילין דמחופות עור, ותניא: הנכנס לבית הכסא חולץ תפילין ברחוק ארבע אמות ונכנס -- tefillin are covered with leather and are still removed before entering a privy
the baraita: one who enters a privy removes his tefillin at a distance of four cubits and enters
R' Oshaya: provided he does not hold it in his hand and carry it four cubits in the public domain
אלמא קסבר עולא -- since he reverses the rulings for a man, each sex's things are unfit for the other
Ulla: and the reverse of these [holds] for a man [i.e. a man is liable for a ring without a seal]
לילה זמן תפילין ושבת זמן תפילין -- הוה ליה מצות עשה שלא הזמן גרמא

התם קסבר רבי מאיר לילה זמן תפילין הוא ושבת זמן תפילין הוא -- for R' Meir tefillin are not time-bound, and women are obligated in them (= p_hatam_rabbi_meir, p_rm_tefillin_shelo_zman_grama, p_nashim_chayavot_shelo_zman_grama)
there [the tefillin baraita] -- R' Meir holds [as follows]
מתיב רב יוסף: הרועים יוצאין בשקין ... ולא הרועים בלבד אמרו אלא כל אדם -- a garment that is one group's way is permitted to any person; so what is fit for one is not unfit for another
shepherds go out in sacks; and not of shepherds alone did they say it but of any person -- only that it is the way of shepherds to go out in sacks

איתיביה אביי: המוצא תפילין מכניסן זוג זוג, אחד האיש ואחד האשה -- and if women are a people unto themselves, tefillin are a time-bound positive mitzva from which women are exempt [so how may a woman bring them in by wearing them?]
one who finds tefillin brings them in pair by pair, a man and a woman alike
והא הוצאה כלאחר יד היא! -- wearing a sealed ring on the finger is carrying out in a backhanded manner, so why is she liable?
but [going out wearing the ring] is carrying out in a backhanded manner
באשה גזברית עסקינן (= p_isha_gizbarit); conceded for a woman but found insufficient for a man by R' Yochanan, after which Rava answers with אלא
אמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יוחנן: תרצת אשה, איש מאי איכא למימר? -- for a man wearing a ring without a seal it is still carrying in a backhanded manner
R' Yirmeya: we are dealing with a woman treasurer
אלא אמר רבא: פעמים שאדם נותן לאשתו טבעת שיש עליה חותם להוליכה לקופסא ומניחתה בידה (= p_rava_isha_lakufsa)
ופעמים שהאשה נותנת לבעלה טבעת שאין עליה חותם להוליכה אצל אומן ... ומניחה בידו (= p_rava_ish_leuman)
Rava: sometimes a man gives his wife a ring with a seal to take to the box, and she puts it on her hand until she reaches the box
R' Meir: [a woman who went out] with a ring that has a seal on it is liable to a sin-offering
Rav Yosef: Ulla holds that women are a people unto themselves
והתניא: רבי אליעזר פוטר בכובלת ובצלוחית של פלייטון! -- elsewhere R' Eliezer only exempts, not permits
R' Eliezer exempts with a kovelet and with a flask of palyaton
לא קשיא: הא כי קאי אדרבי מאיר, הא כי קאי אדרבנן -- 'exempt' answers R' Meir's 'liable', 'permitted' answers the Rabbis' 'exempt but forbidden' (= p_kai_adrabbi_meir, p_kai_aderabanan)
the stam: [the 'exempt'] is when he stands on R' Meir -- against R' Meir, who said liable to a sin-offering, he said exempt
she may not go out with a kovelet
R' Meir holds it is a burden
the mishna: [a woman may not go out] with a kulyar
a woman may not go out with a perforated needle
shiryon is zarda [Steinsaltz: a coat of mail]
